content: Physlib has seen an uptake in activity recently, and I wanted to know what's happening across the board. I vibe-coded a script which reads recent PRs with activity and sends it to Claude to generate a summary, and maybe it's useful for others so I'm posting the output here. If people think this is somewhat useful I can try to run this every week.

Physlib weekly digest (19–26 June)

Physlib weekly digest (19–26 June 2026)

Model: claude-opus-4-8

Infrastructure: the toolchain bump and a framework rename

The headline merge is the Lean v4.31.0 bump (Physlib#1231), touching 216 files across Physlib, PhyslibAlpha and QuantumInfo. It was mostly mechanical deprecation handling, with two gotchas worth noting for downstream authors: convert often needs to become convert!, and attribute [local instance 100] LieRing.ofAssociativeRing is now required in some Lie-algebra contexts. Several open feature branches subsequently had to be re-merged against it.

On the relativity side, PermCond was renamed to IsReindexing (Physlib#1269), moving the tensor-reindexing results into their own directory and restructuring/golfing several proofs (25 files). This is part of a larger tensor-framework cleanup that also produced a representation-based contraction layer (Physlib#1213, the Lorentz-group representation on vectors, now merged) and basis-expansion evaluation lemmas (Physlib#1222, Physlib#1292).

A large-scale linter and golf campaign

Two automation threads dominated PR volume this week.

The first is the QuantumInfo linter rollout. Physlib#1212 brought QuantumInfo under the linters with an exemption file, enabling a file-by-file cleanup. A steady stream of small per-file PRs followed (Physlib#1224, Physlib#1225, Physlib#1229, Physlib#1240, Physlib#1262, Physlib#1273), each adding docstrings and clearing one file. The friction point is Physlib#1244, which tried to de-exempt 59 files at once; the maintainer pushed back that a 50-file PR is effectively unreviewable in a moving codebase and asked for batches of 3–4 files instead — a recurring tension between bulk automation and reviewability.

The second is a wave of AI-assisted proof golfing (the auto-golf / auto-task scripts), shrinking proofs across nearly every module — e.g. Physlib#1259 (harmonic-oscillator uniqueness, 169→51 lines), Physlib#1248 (Wick-algebra ideal membership, 123→19), Physlib#1251 (CKM unitarity), Physlib#1281, Physlib#1271, Physlib#1252. Most merged cleanly. The scripts did expose a coordination gap: Physlib#1234, Physlib#1246 and Physlib#1247 independently golfed the same adiabatic_relation_log proof, prompting a note to add randomisation and a "check existing PRs first" step to the prompts. A much larger manual golf pass, Physlib#1263 (~4,390 net lines removed across 107 files), remains open under review. Alongside these, an API-map.yaml tracking format is being introduced per directory (Physlib#1265 merged; Physlib#1266/Physlib#1267 closed to be regenerated with an improved template).

Physics content

  • Harmonic oscillator initial conditions (nateabr): two-position (Physlib#1217) and two-velocity (Physlib#1250) parametrisations merged, with the amplitude–phase form (Physlib#1294) newly opened — the latter introduces the first use of Complex.arg in ClassicalMechanics to dodge an arctan quadrant split.
  • Spectral theory of unbounded self-adjoint operators (gloges): orthogonal-subspace lemmas (Physlib#1208), spectrum-is-real and trivial-residual-spectrum results (Physlib#1218), and a new SpectralMeasure definition with the projection-multiplication property (Physlib#1239).
  • New API by Robby955: a Galilean group in arbitrary dimension (Physlib#1245), a closed-embedding/closedness result for the Lorentz group (Physlib#1243), a Standard-Model gauge-quotient interface (Physlib#1275), SpaceTime manifold derivatives (Physlib#1278), and the TimeAndSpace coordinate type with its Euclidean and Schwartz-map actions (Physlib#1241, Physlib#1242). The IsManifold instance for Space (Physlib#1176) also landed.
  • Electromagnetism (NicolaBernini): a series of small, steady additions — additive structure and a Lorentz DistribMulAction on the EM potential (Physlib#1256, Physlib#1283), a ToField index-evaluation API for field strength (Physlib#1287), and ongoing refactoring away from FieldStrengthMatrix (Physlib#1288).
  • PhyslibAlpha local classical field theory (juanjfndz): a first-order specialisation layer (Physlib#1235) and a total-divergence Lagrangian API (Physlib#1291), plus a general second-partial-derivative test with a coupled-spring application (Physlib#1226).
  • Sorry-closing (FloWsnr): free-particle momentum/energy conservation (Physlib#1233) and a test-function divergence proof (Physlib#1232).

Active discussions and sticking points

  • Levi-Civita tensor (Physlib#1274): a rank-4 antisymmetric tensor with sign-table definition. Review centred on whether the all-up ε^{0123}=+1 convention and a hand-written sign table are the right long-term choice; the author moved it to its own file and is waiting on input from a domain expert (@wdconinc) before committing to a systematic definition.
  • Fluid dynamics structure (Physlib#1125, and the redirected pressure-field Physlib#1272): coordination on whether general equations (continuity, momentum) should live in a shared FluidDynamics namespace rather than under Navier–Stokes. The maintainer favours the larger restructure; Physlib#1272 was steered to align with this rather than land standalone.
  • N=1 SUSY conjugation foundation (Physlib#1223): a reusable tensor-conjugation layer plus a rebuilt chiral-sector TensorSpecies. Well-received after several review rounds and now approved.
  • IsTotalTimeDerivative redefinition (Physlib#1216): reworks the definition for compatibility with EulerLagrange.lean and proves equivalence with the explicit-formula form; merged after naming and dot-notation cleanups.
  • AI-contribution governance: an agent-review rubric and example GitHub Action (Physlib#1209) remains in draft discussion, building on the AI policy and AGENTS.md merged earlier.

Throughput was high and review turnaround fast, with jstoobysmith handling the bulk of reviews; the main process question raised this week is how to keep automated bulk PRs (linter sweeps, golf passes) small enough to review meaningfully.
